minor.issue: Brute-force lockout spec says 5 fails → 429, but first 429 was only on attempt 9. Root cause: ident = f'{request.client.host}:{email}' and client.host is the ingress IP as seen by each backend pod (different pods for different requests → 10.211.10.135 vs .136 observed in db.login_attempts). Counters are fragmented per-pod so lockout threshold is effectively multiplied by the pod count. Fix: use just the normalized email as identifier (or X-Forwarded-For via a proxy header), and add a unique index on login_attempts.identifier.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout identifier so it works across multiple backend pods — use email (lowercased) as the ident key (optionally include X-Forwarded-For) and create a unique index on login_attempts.identifier to prevent concurrent-upsert fragmentation.

rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout: In auth.py:125 the identifier combines request.client.host with the email. In this environment the ingress proxies requests across at least 2 backend pods and client.host is the ingress hop IP as seen by each pod (10.211.10.135 and 10.211.10.136 observed). Each pod maintains its own counter in login_attempts, so for the same email the counter is split roughly in half (confirmed: 7 wrong attempts gives first 429 on #9–#10 instead of #6). Reproduction: register fresh user, POST /api/auth/login with wrong password; the 429 appears only around attempt 7-10. Mitigation: use email.lower() as the sole identifier (optionally keyed by trusted X-Forwarded-For) and add a unique index on login_attempts.identifier to make upserts race-safe.
